sections.name: Koopa Kid Space
sections.card:
Summary: Landing on one of these spaces brings out a Koopa Kid, who then does one of several nasty things to you or to everyone. Mario Party 7 lets only Bowser and Koopa Kid make them.
Weak points: It goes away if a different Orb is put on its square, if Yoshi and Birdo's Egg Orb is used on it, or if the Star Space moves onto that square.
Looks like: A round green space with a gold border and a gold Koopa Kid face in the middle.
Tips: His possible tricks: a Cursed Mushroom that limits your next roll to 1 to 5, an even split of everyone's coins, a roulette to swap coins or positions with one other player, a shuffle that moves every player, or a shuffle of everyone's Orbs. In Party Cruise Bowser scatters three Koopa Kid Orbs on the board at the start, and more get tossed when someone gets one from an Orb Space or is forced to buy one in Bowser's shop; Koopa Kid uses it at once.

sections.name: Chain Chomps on Pyramid Park
sections.card:
Summary: On Pyramid Park in Party Cruise you take Stars from your rivals by paying for a Chain Chomp ride. The Chain Chomps are found in the board's pyramid doghouses.
Weak points: Only this board has the Snack Orb; it guards you against Chain Chomps for three turns, ending early if one attacks.
Looks like: Most of the Chain Chomps are black, and one red Chain Chomp stands at the top left of the board; it is the one that gives three Dice Blocks.
Tips: A black Chomp charges 10 coins per single Dice Block, or 20 for a pair; the red one charges 10 for three. In the final four turns every price is halved. Rolling matching numbers while riding earns no bonus coins.

sections.name: Bowser Sphinx
sections.card:
Summary: A statue on the left-hand side of Pyramid Park, towards the middle. Stepping on the Green Space before it wakes it, and it takes the visitor for a treasure thief and curses all players with one of three effects picked at random.
Weak points: In Party Cruise the curse is triggered by the Green Space that faces the sphinx, so steer clear of that square to avoid it.
Looks like: A sphinx based on the Great Sphinx of Giza but with Bowser's head, crowned with a nemes whose lappets are striped pink and blue and which carries a Chain Chomp decoration.
Tips: The curse hits every player and is one of three: all coins are pooled and split evenly, every Blue Space turns Red and every Red Space turns Blue for two turns, or Chain Chomp rides are half price for two turns. A Whomp stands on the route to the Bowser Sphinx and wants 10 coins to let you through.

sections.name: Dark Star chests
sections.card:
Summary: A black Star that sits in one of the treasure chests; opening it costs you one Star. On Grand Canal in Party Cruise, one of the four chests Blooper juggles holds it; in Solo Cruise the chests hold five coins and three Dark Stars.
Tips: Once you pick the Dark Star's chest, you cannot refuse what is inside. On Neon Heights in Party Cruise, a Bowser Time event can drop a Dark Star into the chest that held the Bob-omb; pay Koopa Kid to open it and you are stuck with the Dark Star and lose one Star. If the chest with the ordinary Star gets opened first, the Dark Star vanishes. With no Stars you lose nothing here, whereas Mario Party 6 took 20 coins.

sections.name: The Solo Cruise boss minigame
sections.card:
Summary: A boss minigame in which you ride an elevator while Bowser keeps attacking you; the goal is the 100th floor. Only Solo Cruise unlocks it, and it is the sole minigame with that limit.
Weak points: Reaching floor 100 wins, even with Dice Block numbers still unused; a single hit from any attack loses the game on the spot.
Tips: Each turn you have four Dice Blocks to strike, and the climb equals their sum, from 4 up to 40 floors. Past floor 50 a Koopa Kid joins in, with the same attacks as Bowser (a trio of fireballs or a trio of missiles) plus a laser team attack. Solo Cruise records the floor you lost on, so you can continue from it. The minigame is called Bowser's Lovely Lift!

sections.name: Hammer Bro Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb you set on a space as a trap. When a rival stops on it, a Hammer Bro takes ten coins from them, and you receive the coins.
Uses: Place it on a Blue, Red, Character or Koopa Kid Space. Every board has it apart from Pyramid Park and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!
Tips: It never hits its owner, and landing on your own Orb's space pays you five coins. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb ignores traps.

sections.name: Piranha Plant Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: a Piranha Plant chews up any rival who stops on it, and that rival loses half their coins to you.
Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. The Orb Shop charges fifteen coins, and the only boards without it are Pagoda Peak and Windmillville.
Tips: If you are already on the space when a rival arrives, the plant chews the rival only. Landing on your own trap gives you five coins.

sections.name: Spear Guy Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: a Spear Guy robs any rival who stops on it, taking as many coins as a Dice Block roll shows, and hands them to you.
Uses: Set it on any space you choose as a trap. It is on every board but Grand Canal and Neon Heights.
Tips: The Dice Block shows 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins. It takes the place of Mario Party 6's Goomba Orb.

sections.name: Pink Boo Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: Pink Boo robs a rival who stops on it of a Star, or of 20 coins if they hold none, and passes the loot to you.
Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. Pagoda Peak and Windmillville are the only boards without it. Most shops ask 30 coins, and 15 when there is a discount.
Tips: The trap turns the space into a Character Space, and Pink Boo shows up when a rival stops there. If you land on your own trap you get five coins.

sections.name: Kamek Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: when a rival stops on it, Kamek turns up and hands you control of as many as three of that rival's Character Spaces.
Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. It costs ten coins in the Orb Shop, and only Pagoda Peak, Pyramid Park and Windmillville have it.
Tips: Kamek seizes the Character Spaces the victim had put on the board, and Mario Party 7 caps it at three. Landing on your own Thrown Orb space earns you five coins.

sections.name: Zap Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Roadblock Orb with an Amp inside it. It affects any rival who moves over the space, not only one who stops there: the Amp shocks them, and they lose three coins for each space they move beyond it.
Uses: Put it on a space as a roadblock. An Orb hut sells it for 15 coins, and Pagoda Peak, Neon Heights and Windmillville are where it appears.
Tips: The shock is immediate, afterwards the space returns to normal, and roadblocks you placed never hurt you. A player who passes a second Zap Orb while the first is still draining coins gets both effects stacked, and the draining ends if their coins run out.

sections.name: Thwomp Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Roadblock Orb. A rival who moves over the space is squashed by a Thwomp and cannot go further, so their turn ends there.
Uses: Put it on a space as a roadblock. Windmillville, Neon Heights and Pyramid Park are the boards that carry it.
Tips: Metal Mushroom protects a rival: the Thwomp bounces off and the roadblock achieves nothing. Once someone triggers a roadblock it is gone.

sections.name: Metal Mushroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb that turns you to metal so that the Trap Orbs rivals leave on spaces cannot harm you.
Uses: Use it on yourself for protection against rivals' traps. It appears on Windmillville, Pagoda Peak and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!, costing anywhere between 5 and 30 coins.
Tips: As metal you shrug off a Thwomp Orb (it bounces off), kick a Bob-omb Orb away, and watch a Tweester Orb fade out harmlessly.

sections.name: Snack Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb that only Pyramid Park has: use it on yourself, and a bone you throw keeps Chain Chomps off you.
Uses: Use it on yourself before a Chain Chomp comes for you. It lasts three turns, or ends sooner if a Chain Chomp attacks, in which case the bone is thrown for you automatically.
Tips: Anyone else on your space is also safe. In real play the shield covers only two rounds of your rivals' turns: the count drops once you have moved through a Dice Block, yet rivals can use Chain Chomps only in the gaps between your turns.

sections.name: Slow 'Shroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb that makes the Dice Block crawl, letting you choose your roll.
Uses: Use it on yourself, then press the button while the number one step before your target shows. Every board carries it besides Pagoda Peak and Pyramid Park.
Tips: The Dice Block counts upward and starts over after 10. To roll a three, for example, press the button as it shows a two.
